titleStmt.title: To Harriet Shaw Weaver. Friday, 2 December 1921
titleStmt.author: James Joyce

seriesStmt.p: Machine readable texts of the unpublished correspondence of James Joyce

projectDesc.p: James Joyce's unpublished correspondence, collected, annotated, and made available as a digital edition

div.p: Dear Miss Weaver: There has been an endless amount of confusion all these days both about the printing and the séance . The former is now removed but I am certain that had the draft not been paid the printer would have refused to continue. As it is he has waited for confirmation of payment from the bank here before continuing. As for the séance the person who translated the “fragments” to be read went to Germany with them and they arrived only an hour ago in MS. That of the Sirens is so deficient that I shall not allow it to be read. I shall have to work in conjunction with a writer Mr Fargue – a friend of Mr Larbaud’s – on the others which can be made good, he says.

I received your card and the letter with draft for £100 and containing also your gift. I don’t know what to say about your generosity. Please don’t take this letter as an adequate expression of gratitude. I shall write on Sunday when probably I shall have a few hours free. At one time I was patient and goodtempered and polite. Now I have difficulty in preserving these qualities. Perhaps I have tried to do too much in this book. Thank goodness it will soon be out!
I sent you the plan. It is incomplete, made from memory. The one I made is locked up in my case of books.

Thanks for the programme. Yes, it is true that I had a voice (or perhaps have still?). I was, in fact, the rival of Mr John MacCormack McCormack
.

There is an article about Ulysses in the Secolo of Milan – the second Italian daily paper. Of course nobody in Trieste would think it worth his or her while to send it. I shall get it from Milan direct and forward.
I see myself seated on that wheelbarrow, neglecting the work of the garden and reading Ulysses by James Joyce and falling down asleep on one of the grassplots.
With my poor confused thanks for your kindness – It seems to cover me like an aegis at the moment when I am about to collapse finally to everybody’s relief – and kindest regards

div.note: A reading of passages from Ulysses translated into French, held on 7 December 1921 at La Maison des Amis des Livres, 7 rue de l’Odéon. JJ enclosed a handbill for the séance in his letter to Harriet Weaver of 6 December 1921.

The so-called “schema” of Ulysses, an outline of the themes associated with each episode, mentioned also in JJ’s letters to Larbaud of 6 November 1921 (LIII 53), 15 November 1921 (LIII 53), and 26 November 1921 (LIII 54).
JJ and McCormack shared a platform at the concert held on 27 August 1904 at the Ancient Concert Rooms in Dublin (JJ 168).
Silvio Benco, “Un Ulisse irlandese”, Il Secolo (18 November 1921): 3.
